title: SecretFan: Synthesizing Realistic Data without Breaking Privacy
summary: Generates training and test data from a grammar specification rather than from a learned model, using a discriminator only as a constraint that grammar-produced samples must satisfy, so the generator never trains on the confidential records and the released data cannot reproduce them, and reports competitive utility and resemblance on eight datasets at a fraction of the compute a GAN needs. CTGAN is the prior art the design departs from: the paper describes its conditional generator and training-by-sampling as pushing resemblance so far that the model approaches a copy of the original data, leaving it exposed to membership inference, and notes that adding differential privacy to CTGAN buys that back only at the cost of utility.
evidence: Section 2, conditional generators, states that Xu et al. introduced conditional GANs which extract conditions from the original distribution and train by sampling, that the resulting resemblance means the generator learns to make an exact copy of the original data, and that CTGAN therefore remains vulnerable to data leakage and especially to membership inference attacks, adding that CTGAN can be extended with differential privacy at the cost of data utility; section 4 repeats that CTGAN introduced conditions to address mode collapse and that CTAB-GAN later added information loss for imbalanced categorical features; reference [32] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni. CTGAN appears only in the related work; the evaluation compares the proposed approach against its own variants and no CTGAN results row is reported

title: TabDLM: Free-Form Tabular Data Generation via Joint Numerical-Language Diffusion
summary: Handles tables whose columns mix numbers with free-form text such as reviews or clinical notes by running a joint diffusion process over a continuous numerical latent and a discrete language latent, so text fields are generated in step with the structured columns rather than as an afterthought. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN-based and VAE-based baselines it is measured against, and the Shape and Trend fidelity scores it reports are the SDMetrics column-shape and column-pair-trend metrics.
evidence: Section 2 names CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to Xu et al. 2019, as the representative VAE and GAN formulations of tabular generation; section 5 lists CTGAN as the GAN-based baseline and TVAE as one of two VAE-based baselines among eleven compared methods in four categories; the fidelity table reports Shape and Trend per dataset for CTGAN and TVAE and the downstream table their AUC and RMSE against TABDLM; appendix C states the Shape and Trend metrics quantify marginal column-wise similarity and pairwise dependency preservation, footnoted to https://docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics

title: Quantifying Membership Disclosure Risk for Tabular Synthetic Data Using Kernel Density Estimators
summary: Proposes a membership inference framework for tabular synthetic data that fits kernel density estimators to member and non-member distance distributions, recovering the probabilistic output and ROC analysis of shadow-model attacks without retraining any generator, and shows through ROC analysis that datasets judged safe on average accuracy can still leak badly at low false positive rates. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six generators whose output the attack is run against across four datasets, both trained on the real data through the SynthCity framework.
evidence: Section 1 states the framework is evaluated across four real-world datasets and six synthetic data generators spanning several deep generative paradigms, naming GAN-based CTGAN, ADS-GAN and DPGAN, diffusion-based TabDDPM, VAE-based TVAE and a Bayesian network; section 4 states the six generation techniques, including CTGAN [20] and TVAE [20], are trained on the real data and implemented using the SynthCity framework; Table 3 reports membership inference accuracy and F1 per generator on MIMIC-IV, UK Census, Texas-100X and Nexoid, with CTGAN and TVAE columns, and section 5 discusses TVAE-generated UK Census data as the case where member and non-member distances are statistically indistinguishable; reference [20] resolves to Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni

title: Stable and Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Educational Data with Empirical Marginals: A Copula-Based Approach
summary: Proposes NPGC, a nonparametric Gaussian copula synthesizer that anchors each column to its empirical or differentially privatized marginal and carries dependence only through the copula correlation matrix, and introduces a regeneration stability protocol showing that deep generators drift when retrained on their own output over successive iterations while NPGC does not. The whole empirical program runs on SDV: all four baselines are SDV single-table synthesizers at default hyper-parameters, parametric Gaussian copula, CTGAN, TVAE and Copula-GAN, fidelity is the SDMetrics single-table Quality Report overall score over column shapes and column pair trends, and privacy is its discriminator AUC and DCR share.
evidence: Section 4 states NPGC is evaluated against four baseline models implemented using the SDV single-table synthesizers [34], representing parametric copula models, the deep generative models CTGAN and TVAE, and the hybrid Copula-GAN, and that these provide a consistent basis for comparison within the SDV framework; appendix B states all baseline models were implemented using the SDV single-table synthesizers with default SDV hyper-parameters and no additional tuning, and lists TVAE's loss factor as the weighting used in SDV's implementation; the metrics section states fidelity is quantified using the SDMetrics single-table Quality Report [34], summarized by the overall score defined as the mean of Column Shapes and Column Pair Trends, and that privacy is evaluated using discriminator AUC and DCR share, also cited to [34]; section 2.2 cites the Gaussian-copula model in SDV [34] as motivating the copula-based line NPGC extends; reference [34] is Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni, The Synthetic Data Vault, DSAA 2016

title: Generative AI-Based Monte Carlo Simulation for Method Evaluation Using Synthetic Multilevel Data
summary: Sets out a framework for running Monte Carlo simulation studies on AI-generated data that has a multilevel structure, such as students nested in schools, and evaluates how well predictive performance and parameter recovery estimated on synthetic data track the real thing, adding fidelity criteria for within-table, between-table and machine learning utility. CTGAN is one of the two generators the framework is built on, trained on a joined single table after individual-level variables are split into cluster-mean and cluster-demeaned components, then corrected by a new cluster-level consistency alignment step that forces school-level variables to agree within a synthetic school without collapsing their marginals.
evidence: Section 3.3 states the paper trains ClavaDDPM with multiple-table data and CTGAN with join-as-one data and then enhances each with targeted modifications for multilevel generation; section 3.3.2, CTGAN with Cluster-Level Consistency Alignments, restates CTGAN's WGAN-GP minimax objective and refers to Xu et al. 2019 for mode-specific normalization, one-hot encoding and training-by-sampling, then states that because CTGAN is designed for single-table generation it does not preserve hierarchical structure and may assign different school-level values to students in the same school, and introduces cluster-level consistency alignment as a post-processing procedure that enforces identical school-level values while preserving fidelity; section 3.2 states individual-level variables are transformed into cluster-demeaned and cluster-mean components before training; the modifications wrap CTGAN rather than alter its architecture or losses. The bibliography lists DataCebo's Synthetic Data Metrics version 0.12.0 and the text cites SDV as an open-source benchmark for similarity score thresholds

title: MobEvolve: An Agentic Self-Evolving Heuristic System for Interpretable Human Mobility Generation
summary: Generates human trip chains through a system of interpretable heuristics for travel participation, mobility retrieval and refinement that a language model agent rewrites and re-scores against held-out data, so the generator stays readable and cheap while beating deep and LLM-based mobility models on Singapore and Montreal benchmarks. Four SDV single-table synthesizers stand in for the deep tabular generative arm of the comparison, Gaussian Copula, TVAE, Copula-GAN and CTGAN, run from the SDV library and reported on individual, distribution and behaviour metrics as well as generation latency.
evidence: Section 5.1 lists the baselines and names the deep tabular generative models TVAE, Copula-GAN and CTGAN, the last cited to Xu et al. 2019, alongside behaviour-choice and LLM-based methods, with footnote 1 giving https://docs.sdv.dev/sdv; Table 1 reports CTGAN, Copula-GAN and TVAE rows on the individual, distribution, behaviour and overall metrics for Singapore and Montreal, and Table 2 adds Gaussian Copula under traditional mobility models with per-sample latency for all three deep generators; Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni, The Synthetic Data Vault, appears in the bibliography

title: SGN: A Similarity-based Generative Network for Data Generation under Distribution Shift
summary: Trains a generator on a source domain to produce samples aligned with a shifted target domain by learning a shared linear space and a transmission between the two, so that a handful of target samples is enough to augment the target domain usefully, demonstrated on both image and tabular benchmarks. CTGAN and TVAE are the two tabular baselines, implemented from the SDV library with the default structures it states, and the paper attributes their weaker downstream regression and classification results to their being fitted to the source distribution alone.
evidence: Section 4.2 states that for tabular datasets SGN is compared with the two conditional tabular dataset generation methods CTGAN and TVAE, cited to Xu et al. 2019, and that the SDV library is adopted to implement them with the default structures stated in the library; section 4.3 states SGN outperforms CTGAN and TVAE in most cases because they are designed to learn the source-domain distribution and so do not transfer; Table 2 reports regression results and Table 3 F1 scores for CTGAN and TVAE against SGN under decision tree and MLP downstream models on Adult, DryBean, Avila and Electrical source-target pairs
